chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz from Jameel from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to divide his moments between his companions. He would look at this one and look at that one equally.
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet distribute his time among his companions?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) meticulous adherence to *‘adl* (justice) in his personal interactions, ensuring equitable distribution of his gaze and attention among his companions. This practice underscores the Prophetic ideal of balancing spiritual leadership with social fairness, serving as a practical model for communal harmony and preventing feelings of neglect among the faithful.

en.hubeali: H 14841 – Narrated to me Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, who has said:
Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘The Rasool Allahsaww used to divide hissaww moments between hissaww companions. Hesaww would look at this one, and look at that one equally’.
en.sarwar: 394. Narrated to me Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel, who has said: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said:
‘The Rasool Allah (saww) used to divide his (saww) moments between his (saww) companions. He (saww) would look at this one, and look at that one equally’.
